confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on web searches of aggregated cost-of-living data, mainly Numbeo (Nov 2026), Wise, Expatistan and Hikersbay. Numbeo gives a cappuccino at 48 SEK, a domestic draft pint at 70 SEK, an inexpensive meal at 142.5 SEK and a mid-range meal for two at 850 SEK. Wise's USD figures (about $5.12 coffee, $7.56 beer, $15 inexpensive meal, $92 mid-range for two) closely match these. To convert SEK to USD I used about 9.4 SEK per USD. This rate is implied by comparing the Wise USD figures with the Numbeo SEK figures; it is not a separately sourced exchange rate. Cocktail and wine anchors are less certain. They come from general bar-price guides and venue mentions (cocktails about 120-180 SEK, wine by the glass about 90-150 SEK), not from index data, and I used midpoints of about 150 SEK and 110 SEK. Search data is from late 2026, while the target window is July 2026, so price drift is small but not zero. All four accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge. I did not search for them or check any listings. July is peak summer in Gothenburg, and big events such as the Gothia Cup youth football tournament can push up hostel and budget-hotel prices. However, business-hotel rates often ease in summer, so the 3-star estimate has a wide uncertainty band of about ±25%.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink are anchored to Gothenburg-specific aggregated index data. Accommodation is benchmarked against other Nordic secondary cities such as Malmö, Aarhus and Bergen, scaled slightly below Stockholm and Copenhagen to reflect Gothenburg's high-cost but smaller hotel market.
